stories.head: Boulter beats Golubic in under an hour to reach Japan Open quarter-finals
stories.stand: The British eighth seed won 6-2, 6-1 in Osaka and could regain the British number one ranking with a run to the semi-finals.
stories.say: Katie Boulter needed less than an hour to beat Viktorija Golubic six-two, six-one at the Japan Open in Osaka on Wednesday, and is into the quarter-finals.
body: Katie Boulter beat Viktorija Golubic of Switzerland 6-2, 6-1 at the Japan Open in Osaka on Wednesday to reach the quarter-finals.
The eighth seed won in under an hour. After 2-2 in the first set, she won nine games in a row.
Boulter faces either Antonia Ruzic or Kayla Day next. Just Women's Sports reports a semi-final run would return her to British number one, a spot she lost to Sonay Kartal this week.
Boulter said staying patient in the wind was one of the biggest things for her.

stories.head: Kildunne dropped to bench as England make four changes for Canada rematch
stories.stand: John Mitchell has picked Emma Sing at full-back for Friday's WXV Global Series Test after Canada ended England's 41-match unbeaten run.
stories.say: England have dropped Ellie Kildunne to the bench for Friday's rematch with Canada, with Emma Sing at full-back, after last week's defeat ended a forty-one match unbeaten run.
body: England head coach John Mitchell has made four changes for Friday's WXV Global Series Test against Canada, with Ellie Kildunne dropped to the bench.
Emma Sing starts at full-back. Mia Venner comes in on the wing, Helena Rowland at inside centre and Sadia Kabeya at openside flanker.
Canada beat England 24-21 in Toronto on 16 October, ending England's 41-match unbeaten run. Ruck reports Friday's match is in Ottawa.
Mitchell said Kildunne adds huge value but is going through a difficult period, according to Ruck.

stories.head: England's Jasmin Strange ruled out of Rugby League World Cup
stories.stand: The forward hurt her knee in training before Saturday's match against Australia in Perth; Lucy Murray is expected to take her place.
stories.say: England have lost Jasmin Strange for the rest of the women's Rugby League World Cup after she injured her knee in training, ahead of Saturday's match with Australia in Perth.
body: England forward Jasmin Strange will miss the rest of the women's Rugby League World Cup with a knee injury.
Total Rugby League reports she was hurt in training on Tuesday, before Saturday's match against world champions Australia in Perth.
Strange scored a try on her debut in England's 70-6 win over Wales. England will not call up a replacement for now.
Leeds Rhinos' Lucy Murray is expected to take her place. Head coach Stuart Barrow said the side would lose a bit of quality.

stories.head: PSG's Kvaratskhelia to have surgery on ruptured knee ligament
stories.stand: The Georgia winger was hurt in Tuesday's 4-2 win over Barcelona; PSG have given no timetable for his return.
stories.say: Paris Saint-Germain say Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured a knee ligament in Tuesday's win over Barcelona and will have surgery in the coming days.
body: Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament in Tuesday's 4-2 Champions League win over Barcelona.
He went down on his right leg after a challenge from Xavi Espart and was carried off in the 59th minute.
PSG said he would have surgery in the coming days. The club has set no timeline for his return.
CBS Sports notes that such injuries usually keep players out for at least nine months.

stories.head: FIFA bans Egypt coach Hossam Hassan for three matches
stories.stand: The sanction follows his claim that Egypt were cheated out of a World Cup quarter-final against Argentina; Egypt's FA is weighing an appeal.
stories.say: FIFA has banned Egypt coach Hossam Hassan for three matches over his criticism of the refereeing in Egypt's World Cup loss to Argentina. Egypt's FA is considering an appeal.
body: FIFA's disciplinary committee has suspended Egypt head coach Hossam Hassan for three matches over comments after the World Cup.
Hassan said Egypt had been cheated out of a quarter-final place after their 3-2 round-of-16 defeat by Argentina in July.
His brother Ibrahim Hassan, the team manager, was also banned for three matches. Forward Mostafa Zico received a five-match ban for insulting the referee.
The Egyptian Football Association has asked FIFA for its reasons before deciding whether to appeal. Both Hassans could miss November's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Malawi.
